title: Fixed-gradient-flow torus metrics with unchanged geometric-control time and arbitrarily large uniform viscous observation time
difficulty_reason: H3: keeping the gradient vector field, its potential function and the observation set fixed while changing only the viscous metric requires a genuinely geometric spectral construction, not the earlier Euclidean f_lambda counterexample. The author quantizes angular modes with epsilon_k=c/k, proves matching exponential eigenfunction localisation through two complementary energy-propagation estimates and local elliptic interpolation, and obtains weighted final-state versus observation estimates governed by W^c and the effective potential c^2/R^2+|f'|^2/4. The torus metric is then engineered from a positive prescribed effective potential with a unique well so that the drift/GCC travel time stays unchanged while the Agmon barrier and uniform observation-time lower bound grow like delta^(-1/2). This complete semiclassical/geometry-dependent mechanism is research-level; cited standard upper Agmon and spectral-extension inputs remain explicitly attributed rather than re-proved.
